correctness.rationale: In the repaired proof, on each r=±1 input class the normalized expansion modulo 3 is t−(a/3)r with derivative 1 modulo 3, so Hensel gives each whole r+9 Z_3 cylinder. For a=3b the zero-input branch divided by 27 is t^3−bt with derivative −b modulo 3, taking precisely one residue when b=1 modulo 3 and every residue when b=−1. For a=9c direct rescaling gives 27 V_c. Iteration stops at v_3=0 or 1 as stated in the repair; for a=0 the residual nested sets have intersection {0}. For a unit ≡−1 the three normalized derivatives are units and give three disjoint cylinders mod 9. A unit ≡1 is a square and reduces by unit rescaling to F_1, whose positive class is −2+27t²(t+1); t=±1 mod 3 maps onto both attained classes of t²(t+1), giving the two mod-81 cylinders on this branch, their negatives on the other branch, and the distinct 9 Z_3 branch. Their reductions indeed give counts 3,3,5 and then 13·3^(k−4). Counting disjoint reductions and solving δ(9c)=2/9+δ(c)/27 gives the stated phase law with fixed point 3/13. The repaired decreasing-cylinder argument establishes the limiting density. Independent enumeration checked 72 complete finite image sets, at a=0,3,−3,9,18,27,54,81 and k=1…9, not all parameters or depths; the repaired stopping rule is in particular consistent with the checked odd valuations.
